_comment: Container definitions, applied by infra/bootstrap.sh. Mirrors CONTAINERS
in libs/medw_core/cosmos.py - if you change one, change both.
Partition key is the decision that is expensive to reverse: it is fixed at
creation and changing it means creating a new container and migrating. Two
rules drove every choice here - reads must be single-partition, and writes
must spread. /study_id satisfies both for anything scoped to a study;
sessions use /user_id because that read is always per-writer.
Indexing policy is excludePaths, not includePaths. Cosmos indexes every
path by default and you pay RU on writes for each one; excluding the large
free-text fields nobody filters on is most of the write cost back.

containers.name: documents
containers.description: One item per ingested source document: blob path, doc type + classifier confidence, parser version, page count, extraction status.

containers.name: jobs
containers.description: Ingestion job state machine, written by both the Airflow DAG and the synchronous worker so a writer can watch progress on a document they just uploaded.
containers._ttl_note: 30 days. Job state is operational, not evidential - the durable record of what was indexed is audit.index_event in Azure SQL.

containers.name: sessions
containers.description: Writer session: open study, current section, retrieval context of the last few turns. Never the drafted prose - that goes to core.section_draft.
containers._ttl_note: 12 hours. Expiry is the database's job; a cleanup cron is a thing that silently stops running.

containers.name: generations
containers.description: The raw model output plus slots, skeleton and verification detail. High churn, schema varies by template. The distilled, joinable row is audit.generation_event in SQL; this is the fat payload behind it.
containers._ttl_note: 90 days. The audit row in SQL is permanent; the full text of every rejected draft is not.
